seat: director, v2 after owner feedback (concept first, no moving text, finer cloud); one Opus revision round on a director's note; strips and the v2 before/after sheet read at 480x270; commit beat off (D11)

truth.claim: Earth at perihelion 147.095 million km and 30.29 km/s, at aphelion 152.100 million km and 29.29 km/s; distance x speed agrees within 0.011 %
truth.note: measured values (NASA fact sheet), bound twice on stage by the formula; the 0.011 % lands at 53.5 s after both products are counted

truth.claim: 30,000 simulated orbit states (300 planets x 100 moments) land on 6 shells by spin and 5 layers by energy; our planet's 100 dots stay on one shell and in one layer
truth.note: lib/data rebuilt from factory/topics/noether-symmetry by recompute.py and mkdata.py, same seeds; the cut plane is dropped; the followed planet is the picture of 'conserved'

truth.claim: 10,000 training states of a tiny network (100 runs x 100 steps): the weights move 0.24, the fixed sum moves 0.00095, about 250 times less
truth.note: both values on one frame before the ratio

legibility_phone: ok (caption band and readouts at or above 16 units; G6 overflow is the kit shell, not the film)
moves_3d: one orbit, three readouts, the flat bar (0-12 s)
Earth's two measured moments in one panel (27 s)
turn the whole picture under a still readout (42-48 s)
30,000 dots sort by spin into 6 shells (68-80 s)
regroup by energy into layers (88-101 s)

defects.what: the followed planet is faint in the 30,000-dot tangle at thumbnail size (reads at stage size)
the network dots read as short streaks (100 steps per run, close together)
the bar is labelled 'speed around the sun' (the tangential part), which is the honest product; a lay viewer may read it as plain speed

notes: v2 replaces v1 on the same artifact. Text: one readout panel, one corner tag, at most one pin; nothing moves and nothing touches the cloud (checked every 0.5 s by the reviser). Part 1 of a three-part series; Parts 2 and 3 in production.
